label: copy-phase input token c
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input is the letter c (the model just emitted c and now outputs the next original token). Never fires on c during the original phase or the delimiter step, and never on any other input token. Recall is 100%. About 26% of copy-phase c inputs stay inactive, and these misses have no obvious structure (next_out exclusions did not help). The strongest activations come at the first copy step after the first output (recall_idx 1, i.e. c was original token 0 and is followed by c again), and they are boosted when c is repeated (c c): the second c in a run is weaker. Late copies of c in the sequence give low activations.

issues: The core claims hold. All activation mass is in phase 2: 0 active steps in the original phase or at the delimiter, and every active step has in_tok == c. Misses on the test split show 0 missed activations. Precision 0.744 and F1 0.853 are the same on dev and test.

Minor structure in the false positives, which the explanation says it could not find: in short sequences, copy-phase c rarely fires. Precision is 0.174 for L == 3 (n=855) and 0.535 for L == 4, against about 0.76 for L >= 8. Precision is also lower at recall_idx == 1, where the fed-back c follows <DEL> (0.616). The rest of the false positives look scattered: precision stays at 0.70-0.79 across subsets by prev_tok vowels or digits, next_out digits, in_count >= 2, n_digits >= 3 and the last step.

The magnitude claim is overstated. The c inputs at recall_idx >= 5 cover the activation quartiles at 0.35 / 0.33 / 0.31 / 0.25, lowest to highest. They lean only slightly toward low activations, so 'late c inputs mostly give low activations' is too strong. c inputs at recall_idx <= 2 do lean somewhat toward the top quartile (0.41 coverage). The claim that the first c of a 'c c' run is strongest matches the top examples. For prev_tok == c, precision is 0.594 and the inputs sit slightly more in the lower quartiles.
A length gate barely helps on test. Adding L >= 4 gives F1 0.856 and adding t >= 6 gives 0.857, against a baseline of 0.853. Neither is a meaningful fix.
